messages:
Maya (People Ops): Thanks everyone — reposting a few folks' follow-ups from today's all-hands about reviews/promos/benefits. I'll collect quick answers here. Drop any manager-specific scenarios.

Sam (Eng Manager): Two quick ones — 1) How do we handle performance notes for someone who was on parental leave during review window? 2) Someone changed manager mid-cycle — whose calibration do they go into?

Alex (IC): Also, will new hire equity vesting changes affect promotion comp targets if hire was <6 months?

Lena (People Ops): Short answers: 1) People on approved parental leave are still included; we use manager input + backup reviewer if manager is OOO. We won't penalize leave. 2) Mid-cycle manager changes: employee follows the new manager for calibration but we carry forward original feedback; we tag both managers in calibration packet.

Chris (Director, Eng): To add — if new manager joined within last 2 weeks, we pair with peer manager for context.

Dana (Manager): What about retroactive promos? If we approve a promo but it triggers budget constraints, what's the timing for comp changes?

Ethan (Finance): If promo approved within window it gets effective date as of the promo approval; comp changes appear in next payroll cycle (we'll post calendar). Retroactive pay is limited to exceptional cases; need finance+peopleops signoff.

HR Bot: <link> Benefits enrollment window: https://redwood/reports/benefits-open-enrollment FY27

Lena (People Ops): Promo paperwork cutoff is EOD the day before final calibration. For after-cutoff cases, we can process but it goes into next cycle. Exceptions for org changes/merges handled case-by-case.

Sam (Eng Manager): Example: direct report went on leave Feb 10, review window Feb 1-28. Manager couldn't meet for calibration. Process?

Maya (People Ops): For that case: manager submits written calibration notes with last 60 days of performance, tags backup reviewer or skip-level, and we include note 'on leave' in packet. No negative default.

Alex (IC): Clarify leveling appeals timeline? How long do ICs have to appeal rating or banding?

Lena (People Ops): ICs have 10 business days after system rating posted to submit appeal. Appeals go to People Ops + neutral review panel; decision within 14 business days typically.

Dana (Manager): Are there guardrails around promotion frequency? e.g., moving from L3->L4 within 9 months.

Chris (Director, Eng): Generally minimum 12 months between promotions unless exceptional (leadership role change or org need). Exception requires director+PeopleOps approval.

Maya (People Ops): We'll drop a short FAQ doc and a template for 'manager mid-cycle handoff' in #docs. Tagging folks: @Sam, @Dana please DM if you have specific cases and we'll help with packet.

Lena (People Ops): Quick note: compensation bands will be updated after annual market comp review — expect band midpoints tweaked in April; we'll send memo.

Sam (Eng Manager): Thanks — very helpful :thumbsup:
